messages:
maya: noticed a burst of 502/504 reports from multiple tenants about 16:40 UTC, hosted-api edge. customer A saw ~8% request failures for 3m, spike correlates with a keystore rollout. sample trace: trace=trc-8f3c2b. can we triage?
jonathan: looking now — any request ids or curl samples from a repro? is this only streaming endpoints or regular generation too?
maya: both; streaming more visible. quick curl a sample gave a 502 intermittently. req-id: req-0a1b2c.
liam: grabbing envoy logs for that trace. past 10m I see a pattern: upstream reset after connect timeout then 502 sent back. snippet: 
```
[2026-03-20T16:39:52.123Z] envoy upg: upstream 10.20.5.14:443 connect timeout
[2026-03-20T16:39:52.124Z] router: cluster outbound|model-srv|green upstream reset, code=CONNECT_TIMEOUT
[2026-03-20T16:39:52.124Z] response sent: HTTP/1.1 502
```
maya: that matches customer curl: sometimes 502, sometimes 504.
jonathan: any recent infra changes? I saw a keystore rotation job around 16:35 that updated TLS client certs for upstream model pools. could that cause connection failures during handshake?
ingress-oncall: I executed a keystore rollout to rotate internal clients at 16:33 (audit id ks-20260320). We saw a small spike in TLS handshakes failing on a subset of model pool nodes; health checks kept marking them degraded. I just paused the rollout at 16:46.
maya: can you paste the healthcheck logs?
ingress-oncall: health probe log: 
```
probe: GET /healthz -> 200
probe: TLS handshake error: tls: private key does not match public key
node=pool-3-7
```
liam: ok that explains CONNECT_TIMEOUT then 502. Envoy tried but upstream refused due to bad cert. impact: any requests routed to pool-3-7 got connection failures; routing is weighted so overall failure rate ~5-10% depending on fanout.
jonathan: mitigation: revert keystore on pool-3 and restart its model-serving process to clear bad certs. also, we should add rolling verification to the rollout (verify handshake post-update before switching live).
maya: can we also increase upstream connect timeout window temporarily to reduce 502s during the drain? maybe not ideal but reduces customer-facing spikes.
ingress-oncall: I rolled back ks-20260320 on pool-3 at 16:50 and restarted the node; correlation: error rate dropped to baseline by 16:54.
deploy-bot: deploy rollback ks-20260320 -> pool-3 completed (job id rb-4421).
liam: follow-ups: 1) add preflight check for keystore rotations (small TLS probe against each node post-update), 2) ensure envoy health check threshold is slightly more forgiving during controlled rollouts, 3) run customer-visible post-check (sample request) before marking rollout healthy.
jonathan: i've filed a runbook PR with steps and curl examples to repro/verify: 
```
# repro curl (non-streaming)
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  https://hosted.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
# look for 502/504 and record x-request-id
```
maya: customer notified and support ticket updated — they confirmed improvement after rollback. closing after postmortem. :thumbsup:
ingress-oncall: adding a follow-up task to infra backlog: KEYSWAP-11 - add canary tls-probe + alerting.
liam: recording timeline for postmortem. thanks all
